barrier_or_finding: Poor performance status may prevent clinicians from offering TTFields
population_or_design: Retrospective single-institution review; 178 records (2015–2022), 96 offered, 82 not offered
reported_result: Among those not offered, 66% were reported not offered because of poor KPS
commercial_or_clinical_implication: Do not interpret low prescription rates without an eligibility and KPS denominator
evidence_strength_and_limitations: Single center, retrospective, historic data; does not define universal eligibility or payer rules
proposed_metric: Offer rate stratified by KPS and predefined eligibility
recommended_response: Record reasons for non-offer; do not equate non-offer with refusal

barrier_or_finding: Clinician-perceived barriers include practical treatment burden, insufficient social support and adherence concerns
reported_result: Oncologist-reported barriers: physical difficulty 62%, lack of support system 60%, adherence concerns 58%; patient/caregiver barrier: concern about later clinical-trial eligibility 64%; only 26% recalled discussing long-term survival data although 92%/90% of oncologists reported often/always discussing 2-/5-year data
commercial_or_clinical_implication: Counseling and service support can shape initiation; patient and clinician recollections of discussions may differ
evidence_strength_and_limitations: Sponsor-affiliated Novocure Thought Leader Liaison authors; survey/abstract, not independent national practice census
proposed_metric: Proportion of eligible patients discussed; patient understanding; clinician-reported reasons for non-recommendation
recommended_response: Balanced decision support, staff training and payer navigation

barrier_or_finding: Patients may report delayed or incomplete discussions and self-advocacy burden
population_or_design: National survey; 525 respondents, 77% caregivers and 23% patients
reported_result: Younger patients more likely to report offer; NCI-center patients and male patients more likely to report first-line offer; delayed discussions and self-advocacy described
commercial_or_clinical_implication: Offer and timing should be audited, not assumed uniform across centers or demographic groups
evidence_strength_and_limitations: Conference supplement abstract; self-reported, non-probability sample with high private-insurance and NCI-center share
proposed_metric: Rate of documented discussion and first-line offer stratified by center and demographics
recommended_response: Standardized patient discussion and referral triggers

barrier_or_finding: Some respondents report no discussion and financial/insurance difficulty
reported_result: 40% reported no TTFields discussion; of those trying to access, 29% reported difficulty, often financial/insurance related
commercial_or_clinical_implication: Information and coverage navigation can influence access
evidence_strength_and_limitations: Conference abstract and self-selected online survey; different sample from 2025 n=525
proposed_metric: Documented discussion, denial/appeal rate, start conversion
recommended_response: Earlier balanced discussion and payer-specific assistance

barrier_or_finding: Device can substantially restrict daily activities while some patients remain willing to continue
population_or_design: Two-center observational PRO study; 30 high-grade glioma patients receiving TTFields+chemotherapy
reported_result: 71% affected in daily life at least 2–3 times per week; restrictions included device duration, size/weight, array changing, body care, work/hobbies and relationships; 70% would recommend, 67% would reuse
commercial_or_clinical_implication: Burden is multidimensional; it is not synonymous with unwillingness or non-adherence
evidence_strength_and_limitations: Small sample; mixed high-grade glioma cohort; PRO at two months
proposed_metric: Validated treatment-burden and HRQoL score; array-change time; activity restrictions
recommended_response: Pre-treatment expectation setting, practical training and individualized support

barrier_or_finding: Spousal support associated with higher initiation in one cohort
reported_result: 58% initiation among patients with spousal support vs 47% without documented spousal support
commercial_or_clinical_implication: Social support may affect practical feasibility
evidence_strength_and_limitations: Associational result; does not establish causality or justify family-status eligibility rules
proposed_metric: Start rate by available support; reported unmet support need
recommended_response: Offer caregiver-inclusive training and alternative support services

barrier_or_finding: Adherence burden, finances and scalp toxicity documented among patients discontinuing after concurrent CRT
population_or_design: Six-center retrospective cohort; 100 patients treated during concurrent CRT; 32 stopped after CRT
reported_result: Among 32 discontinuers: adherence burden 44% (14), financial constraints 28% (9), mild scalp toxicity 16% (5), physician recommendation 9% (3), other 3% (1)
commercial_or_clinical_implication: Sustainability can fail after initial start, especially when costs shift to patient
evidence_strength_and_limitations: Small non-randomized cohort; specific country/payment context; discontinuers selected by design
recommended_response: Track costs and use burden beyond initiation; improve skin-care escalation

barrier_or_finding: Questions raised about sham controls, comparators, dosimetry and post-market transparency
reported_result: Argues no sham-controlled RCT has isolated device effect from service/support package; identifies comparator and reporting issues
adoption_stage_affected: Clinician confidence / guideline adoption / patient counseling
commercial_or_clinical_implication: Evidence debate may influence clinician recommendation and informed consent
evidence_strength_and_limitations: Perspective article, not a new RCT; evaluate claims against original trials and guidelines
proposed_metric: Clinician confidence survey; protocol adherence and post-market reporting completeness
recommended_response: Transparent evidence appraisal and independent replication

barrier_or_finding: Financial constraints can stop therapy after it has begun
population_or_design: Retrospective cohort and separate patient/caregiver survey
reported_result: 28% of 32 discontinuers cited financial constraints in the 2026 cohort; 29% of survey respondents attempting access reported difficulty, often financial/insurance-related
commercial_or_clinical_implication: Measure patient liability and financial interruptions, not only insurance approvals
evidence_strength_and_limitations: Different populations and designs; figures must not be pooled
proposed_metric: Denial rate, appeal success, patient OOP, financial reason-specific stop rate
recommended_response: Benefit investigation, transparent liability, affordability support

barrier_or_finding: TTFields offer and timing vary with treatment setting and respondent characteristics
reported_result: NCI-center patients more likely to report a first-line offer; younger patients more likely to report being offered treatment; male patients more likely to report first-line offer
commercial_or_clinical_implication: Center pathways and patient characteristics should be audited for access gaps
evidence_strength_and_limitations: Observational association; no causal interpretation or representative national prevalence
proposed_metric: Offer and start rates by center type, age, sex, insurance and geography
recommended_response: Standardize offer documentation and investigate unexplained gaps
